blocks.heading: Trade unions
blocks.text: A trade union is a group of workers who join together to ensure their interests are protected. It can represent members on pay, conditions and workplace concerns, providing a collective voice and advice. It is distinct from an employer association, which represents employers, and from a friendship group formed for social contact. Representation can help organise concerns and negotiation, but membership does not guarantee that every demand will be accepted. The union and employer can have common interests in a viable workplace while disagreeing about how income, time or risk should be shared.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Fictional Hela Works’ members ask their union to raise a concern about shift arrangements with management. The union represents worker interests in the discussion. It is not the business owner merely because it speaks collectively for employees.
